newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African govt to announce forex caps at 1400 GMT.
newsitem.headline: S.African govt to announce forex caps at 1400 GMT.

text.p: South African Finance Minister Trevor Manuel will make an announcement on the amount of capital private individuals will be allowed to invest abroad at a news conference in Pretoria at 4.00 p.m. (1400 GMT) on Wednesday, the finance ministry said.

Individuals will be allowed to invest offshore for the first time from July 1 but the government has not yet declared how much money they will be able to take out of the country or hold in foreign exchange accounts with local banks.

However, both Manuel and Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals have said in recent weeks that the limit is likely to be set at around 160,000 rand, equivalent to the annual travel allowance for a married couple.
Uncertainty about the impact of the July 1 relaxation has dominated trading in South Africa's financial markets recently.

Investors are nervous that the move could trigger an outflow of capital, although a build-up in official reserves to record levels and the negotiation of foreign credit lines has convinced many that Pretoria is well-equipped to stand such a shock.
